# Sequence addresses

The spine is not only an ordering. Every prefix of it is an address, and every address names a module that loads — `a432.1`, `a432.1.2`, `a432.1.2.4`, on to the closure. The handle carries no payload; the name is the coordinate and the load happens at will.

Occupancy is read off the filesystem, so a module that goes missing appears here as a gap rather than as a sentence that stayed true:

```
● a432.1.ts
● a432.1.2.ts
● a432.1.2.4.ts
● a432.1.2.4.8.ts
● a432.1.2.4.8.7.ts
● a432.1.2.4.8.7.5.ts
● a432.1.2.4.8.7.5.3.ts
● a432.1.2.4.8.7.5.3.6.ts
● a432.1.2.4.8.7.5.3.6.9.ts
● a432.1.2.4.8.7.5.3.6.9.1.ts
```

Kernel spine `124875369` closed on its first digit: **10/10** addressed.

Doubling orbit `124875` closed on its first digit: **7/7** addressed.

Gaps: **0**.

Four kernel sequences are not address spaces at all, and that is a statement rather than a gap — `VORTEX_AXIS` (`369`), `VORTEX_MIRROR`, `VORTEX_REVERSE` and `LEGACY_CONSCIOUSNESS_SEQUENCE` (`0369124875`) have no file at any prefix. They are readings of the walk, not walks; a reading has nowhere to arrive.

The addresses are audited by `npm run a432:names`, filled by `npm run a432:orbit`, and no page may spell a kernel sequence differently from the kernel — `npm run sequence:check`.

See [SEQUENCE.md](../SEQUENCE.md) · [Sequence dual](./sequence-dual.md).
